analysis:
The supplied changes are comment-only edits in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (lines 201-204) and EngineV2KVSizing.swift (lines 8-10), plus test and fixture updates. The test updates in SegmentedProductionGrantTests.swift (82-84) and SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift expect GPT-OSS KV rows to be bf16 on every layer, giving a native rate of 24,576 bytes per token rather than 49,152.

No executable production code is changed in the supplied units. The functions nativeKVBytesPerToken and processKVBytesPerToken keep identical logic, so nothing here weakens the encrypted prefix cache (T-041), the coordinator and provider boundary (TB-002), or attestation. No auth, crypto, key handling, or data-exposure paths are touched.

The comments now say production slots price observed native per-layer types through EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken. That function is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it. The behavior described by the comments and tests depends on it: if GPT-OSS actually stored fp32 KV while the accounting assumed bf16, the admission and KV budget would under-reserve memory and could cause a resource-exhaustion or availability problem, in the T-016 / T-029 class. This is an unverified contract, not a demonstrated regression. The next pass should check that slot assembly really derives per-token cost from the observed dtypes, and that the paged pool dtypes match the admission dtypes.
